items.title: James Lincoln Collier interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007
items.q: You’d listen to the great black saxophone player, Coleman Hawkins, Lester Young, all these guys.

ctx.x: Was there a distinction with you guys in your listening between black and white bands or black and white artists?

Nobody even knew. Nobody cared. The black and white thing didn’t exist. It did not exist. You were — you know Johnny Hodges would be, you know everybody’s favorite alto player. Nobody ever heard of a baritone sax player better than Harry Carney. Louis of course. But you would listen to Louis and you would turn around and listen to Beiderbecke who was white. You would listen to Jack Teagarden and you’d turn around and listen to Dickie Wells who was black. You’d listen to the great black saxophone player, Coleman…
How many people in your fraternity had record players?
